complete_examples.text: Therefore, it is a necessary to conduct a reliability assessment for a specific railway line.

Then, the methodologies for determining the limits of track irregularities and achieving a reliability assessment are presented by introducing the probability density evolution method and development of a Wavelet-Wigner-Hough method.

Furthermore, a vehicle-track coupled model is presented to obtain the dynamic responses of vehicle-track systems due to the earthquakes and track random irregularities at time-domain, and the probability density evolution method (PDEM) is introduced to describe the evolutionary process of probability from excitation input to response output by assuming the vehicle-track system as a probabilistic conservative system, which lays the foundation on reliability assessment of vehicle-track systems.

Conventionally, it has already been a very complex problem to estimate the second-order statistics, not to mention obtaining the probability density distribution of the dynamic indices in the time-dependent reliability assessment.
Concerning the specification of wheel–rail forces, one can obviously figure out that there exist great divergences for reliability assessment of dynamic indices.
